title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 21.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers
questions.explanation: This event is recorded first in the chapter, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:1.

questions.question: Who was buried in the city of David according to 2 Chronicles 21?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat is the one who was buried in the city of David, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:1.

questions.question: How many brethren did Jehoshaphat have?
questions.correctAnswer: Six
questions.explanation: The verse lists six sons of Jehoshaphat, as seen in 2 Chronicles 21:2.

questions.question: What gifts did Jehoshaphat give to his sons?
options: Great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things
questions.correctAnswer: Great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat gave his sons great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:3.

questions.question: Who did Jehoram slay when he became king?
questions.correctAnswer: His brethren
questions.explanation: Jehoram slew all his brethren when he rose to the kingdom, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:4.

questions.question: How old was Jehoram when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: 32 years
questions.explanation: Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, according to 2 Chronicles 21:5.

questions.question: How long did Jehoram reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight years
questions.explanation: Jehoram reigned eight years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:5.

questions.question: Who was Jehoram's wife?
questions.correctAnswer: The daughter of Ahab
questions.explanation: Jehoram had the daughter of Ahab to wife, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 21:6.

questions.question: What was Jehoram's behavior according to the text?
options: He wrought that which was evil
He was obedient to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He wrought that which was evil
questions.explanation: Jehoram did that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:6.

questions.question: Why would the LORD not destroy the house of David?
options: Because of the covenant with David
Because of the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the covenant with David
questions.explanation: The LORD would not destroy the house of David because of the covenant made with David, according to 2 Chronicles 21:7.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise concerning David's house?
options: To give a light to him and his sons forever
To make them a great nation
questions.correctAnswer: To give a light to him and his sons forever
questions.explanation: The LORD promised to give a light to David and his sons forever, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:7.

questions.question: Is it true that Jehoram's reign lasted longer than ten years?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jehoram reigned for eight years, as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:5, which is less than ten years.

questions.question: Is it true that Jehoshaphat had many sons?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat had several sons, specifically listed as six in 2 Chronicles 21:2.

questions.question: Is it false that Jehoram was the last king of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention that Jehoram was the last king of Israel; it states he reigned in Judah.

questions.question: Is it false that Jehoram was a faithful servant of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 21:6, Jehoram wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD, indicating he was not a faithful servant.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the significant event involving the Edomites during Jehoram's reign?
options: They made themselves a king and revolted from Judah's dominion
They allied with Judah against Israel
They were conquered and enslaved by Judah
They built a temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They made themselves a king and revolted from Judah's dominion
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:8 states that the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah and made themselves a king.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 21:10 promise will happen if someone forsakes the LORD God of their fathers as Jehoram did?
options: The people will revolt against them
They will be blessed with long life
They will find favor among the nations
questions.correctAnswer: The people will revolt against them
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:10 links the revolt of Edom and Libnah to Jehoram forsaking the LORD God of his fathers.

questions.question: How did Jehoram respond to the Edomites' revolt?
options: He rose up by night with his princes and chariots and smote the Edomites
He asked for help from Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He rose up by night with his princes and chariots and smote the Edomites
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:9 explains Jehoram's military action against the Edomites by night with his princes and chariots.

questions.question: What is the connection between Jehoram's actions in 2 Chronicles 21:6 and the consequences described in 2 Chronicles 21:14?
options: His evil ways led to a great plague sent by the LORD
His righteousness brought peace and prosperity
His alliances with Israel secured his kingdom
His construction of high places pleased God
questions.correctAnswer: His evil ways led to a great plague sent by the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:6 shows Jehoram's evil deeds, and 21:14 foretells a plague as divine punishment for his sins.

questions.question: What caused Libnah to revolt from under Jehoram's hand according to 2 Chronicles 21:10?
options: Jehoram forsaking the LORD God of his fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoram forsaking the LORD God of his fathers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:10 clearly states Libnah's revolt was because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers.

questions.question: What was one of Jehoram's actions that caused Judah and Jerusalem to 'go a whoring'?
options: He made high places in the mountains of Judah
He built a new temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He made high places in the mountains of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:11 states Jehoram made high places which caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication.

questions.question: Whose ways did Jehoram walk in, according to the writing from Elijah?
options: The way of the kings of Israel
The way of Asa king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The way of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:13 says Jehoram walked in the way of the kings of Israel, unlike his ancestors Jehoshaphat and Asa.

questions.question: What serious accusation did Elijah's letter make against Jehoram concerning his family?
options: He had slain his brethren of his father's house
He had honored all his family members
He had built palaces for his brothers
questions.correctAnswer: He had slain his brethren of his father's house
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:13 states that Jehoram had slain his brethren of his father's house, who were better than himself.

questions.question: What was the LORD's reason for not destroying the house of David during Jehoram’s evil reign?
options: Because of the covenant He had made with David
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the covenant He had made with David
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:7 explains that the LORD did not destroy David's house because of the covenant and promise to David and his sons.

questions.question: How long did Jehoram reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:5 states that Jehoram reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was Jehoram's age when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty-two years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:5 records that Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: What role did the princes play when Jehoram fought against the Edomites?
options: They went out with Jehoram and his chariots to fight
They stayed in Jerusalem to defend the city
questions.correctAnswer: They went out with Jehoram and his chariots to fight
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:9 states that Jehoram went forth with his princes and all his chariots against the Edomites.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoram was blessed by God for continuing the righteous ways of his father Jehoshaphat.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:12-13 reveals that Jehoram did not walk in the ways of Jehoshaphat but in the ways of Israel’s kings, causing judgment.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD sent a writing through Elijah the prophet to Jehoram warning him of consequences because of his evil deeds.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:12 confirms that Elijah sent a writing from the LORD to Jehoram warning about the plague as a consequence of his actions.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoram was known for walking in the righteous ways of Asa and Jehoshaphat and was praised for it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:12-13 clearly states that Jehoram did not walk in the ways of Asa or Jehoshaphat but in the evil ways of Israel’s kings.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 21:15, what was the nature of Jehoram's sickness?
options: Great sickness by disease of the bowels until they fell out
Fever and chills day by day
questions.correctAnswer: Great sickness by disease of the bowels until they fell out
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:15 explicitly states that Jehoram would have great sickness by disease of his bowels until they fell out day by day.

questions.question: Who did the LORD stir up against Jehoram according to 2 Chronicles 21:16?
options: The Philistines and the Arabians near the Ethiopians
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines and the Arabians near the Ethiopians
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:16 states the LORD stirred up the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians near the Ethiopians against Jehoram.

questions.question: What happened to Jehoram’s possessions and family during the invasion described in 2 Chronicles 21:17?
options: They were carried away except Jehoahaz, the youngest son
All were spared except Jehoram himself
Only his wives were taken captive, sons remained
None were taken; they repelled the invaders
questions.correctAnswer: They were carried away except Jehoahaz, the youngest son
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:17 tells that invaders broke into Judah and took all substances, sons, and wives, leaving only Jehoahaz, the youngest son.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 21:18, how is the disease that afflicted Jehoram described?
options: As an incurable disease in his bowels
As leprosy spreading over his body
questions.correctAnswer: As an incurable disease in his bowels
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:18 specifically says the LORD smote Jehoram in his bowels with an incurable disease.

questions.question: How long did Jehoram reign in Jerusalem as stated in 2 Chronicles 21:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:20 clearly states Jehoram reigned in Jerusalem eight years.

questions.question: What unusual detail about Jehoram’s burial is noted in 2 Chronicles 21:20?
options: He was buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchers of the kings
He was buried in a foreign land
He was cremated instead of buried
He was buried with great honor in the royal tombs
questions.correctAnswer: He was buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchers of the kings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:20 notes that although Jehoram was buried in the city of David, he was not buried in the sepulchers of the kings, highlighting a dishonorable burial.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chole' (חֹלֶה) in 2 Chronicles 21:15 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Sickness or disease
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chole' (חֹלֶה) used in 2 Chronicles 21:15 refers to sickness or disease, describing Jehoram’s grievous illness.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the progression of Jehoram's punishment from invasion to incurable disease in 2 Chronicles 21:15-19?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The passage from 2 Chronicles 21:15-19 exhibits chiasmus, a literary structure where the order of ideas is reversed to emphasize the central point: Jehoram's downfall through sickness follows the invasion and captivity.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of divine punishment through disease as found in 2 Chronicles 21:15-18?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 24:15
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:15 describes a plague sent by God as punishment, echoing the divine-inflicted disease on Jehoram in 2 Chronicles 21:15-18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage can be seen as a fulfillment or contrast to the covenant promise mentioned in 2 Chronicles 21:7 about the house of David?
questions.explanation: Luke 1:32-33 speaks of Jesus as a descendant of David whose kingdom will endure forever, fulfilling the covenant promise in 2 Chronicles 21:7 that God would give a light to David and his sons forever.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the LORD’s pronouncement of Jehoram's punishment in 2 Chronicles 21:14?
options: Jehoram’s killing of his brothers and walking in the way of Israel’s kings
Jehoram’s successful military campaign against Edom
Jehoram’s building of high places in Jerusalem
Jehoram’s marriage to the daughter of Ahab
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoram’s killing of his brothers and walking in the way of Israel’s kings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:12-13 shows that before the LORD’s punishment announcement in 21:14, Jehoram killed his brothers and walked in the evil ways of Israel’s kings.

questions.question: How does the disease and punishment of Jehoram in 2 Chronicles 21:15-19 serve as typology in biblical literature?
options: It prefigures divine judgment on unfaithful leaders
It symbolizes the cleansing of sin through suffering
It exemplifies the resurrection from death
It illustrates God’s mercy in healing
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures divine judgment on unfaithful leaders
questions.explanation: Jehoram’s disease and punishment typologically represent divine judgment on kings who forsake God, a theme common in biblical narrative as seen in 2 Chronicles 21:15-19.

questions.question: In the context of 2 Chronicles 21, what is the significance of Jehoram not being buried in the sepulchers of the kings?
options: It signifies dishonor due to his evil reign and covenant unfaithfulness
It indicates his exile from Jerusalem
It reflects his voluntary renunciation of kingship
It was a custom for all kings who reigned less than ten years
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies dishonor due to his evil reign and covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:20 implies that Jehoram’s burial outside the royal sepulchers was a mark of disgrace due to his evil deeds and failure to uphold God’s covenant.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 21:16, the LORD stirred up the spirit of the Moabites and Ammonites against Jehoram.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:16 specifies the LORD stirred up the Philistines and Arabians near the Ethiopians, not the Moabites and Ammonites.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 21:19 states that Jehoram died after his bowels fell out due to his incurable disease.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:19 explicitly states that after two years, Jehoram’s bowels fell out because of his sickness and he died of sore diseases.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 21:7 teach about God's nature in relation to covenant faithfulness despite human sin?
options: God unconditionally blesses all descendants regardless of their actions
God's covenant with David ensures preservation of his lineage despite judgment on sin
God ignores covenant promises when kings sin
God reestablishes new covenants with each king based on their merits
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant with David ensures preservation of his lineage despite judgment on sin
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:7 explicitly states that the LORD would not destroy the house of David because of the covenant He made with David, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His promises even when the king sins.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and human sinfulness is demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 21:14?
options: God's judgment is limited to the individual sinner alone
God's judgment can extend to the sinner's family and possessions
God's judgment is always immediate and final without warning
God does not use physical affliction as a form of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment can extend to the sinner's family and possessions
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:14 shows that the LORD will smite the people, children, wives, and goods, indicating that divine judgment can impact not only the sinner but also his household and possessions.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the consequences of idolatry and apostasy is taught in 2 Chronicles 21:10?
options: Idolatry has no political or social consequences
Forsaking God leads to loss of political authority and territorial control
Judah's kingship was strengthened through apostasy
Divine punishment is only spiritual, not affecting physical realms
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking God leads to loss of political authority and territorial control
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explains that Libnah revolted because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers, showing that apostasy results in loss of political dominion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 21:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:7 emphasizes God's covenant faithfulness in not destroying David's house despite the king's evil actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in 2 Chronicles 21:16 by God's orchestration of the Philistines and Arabians against Jehoram?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:16 shows God stirring up nations against Jehoram, demonstrating His sovereign control over all peoples and events.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 21:4–6 connect to the broader biblical theme of the consequences of apostasy in Israel's monarchy?
options: It shows that apostasy leads to immediate divine blessing
It prepares for the exile by demonstrating the destructive effects of idolatry and fratricide
It contradicts the Deuteronomic promise of prosperity for kings
It illustrates the success of foreign alliances in safeguarding the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares for the exile by demonstrating the destructive effects of idolatry and fratricide
questions.explanation: Verses 4–6 show Jehoram's evil acts and idolatry, echoing themes that lead to judgment and exile later in Israel’s history.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 21:8–10 foreshadow the ultimate loss of Israelite sovereignty in the Old Testament narrative?
options: By showing the strengthening of Judah's political control
By illustrating the beginning of territorial fragmentation due to unfaithfulness
By highlighting the peace and prosperity under Jehoram's reign
By prophesying the future rise of David's dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating the beginning of territorial fragmentation due to unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The revolts of Edom and Libnah in these verses symbolize the fracturing of the kingdom as a consequence of Jehoram’s apostasy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 21:11 and 21:13 teach about human sin and its impact on community worship and leadership?
options: Sin in leadership has limited effect on people's spiritual condition
Leadership sin can lead a community to idolatry and moral corruption
Communities are unaffected by their leaders' moral failures
Idolatry is only a private matter with no communal consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership sin can lead a community to idolatry and moral corruption
questions.explanation: Verse 11 describes Jehoram making high places and causing Jerusalem to sin, while verse 13 highlights his leading Judah into spiritual whoredom, showing how sin in leadership corrupts the whole community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 21:14 and 21:18 teach about the nature of divine judgment and affliction?
options: Divine judgment is always swift and merciful
God's judgment can include prolonged physical suffering as a consequence of sin
Suffering is never related to sin or divine discipline
God only judges through external political defeat
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment can include prolonged physical suffering as a consequence of sin
questions.explanation: Verse 14 announces a great plague and verse 18 specifies Jehoram's incurable disease, indicating that divine judgment may manifest as enduring physical affliction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 21:12 and 21:13 teach about prophetic warning and the consequences of rejecting God's ways?
options: Prophetic warnings are optional and have no real consequence
Ignoring prophetic warnings leads to societal and familial destruction
Prophets only predict future blessings without threats
Rejecting God results in immediate forgiveness without punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring prophetic warnings leads to societal and familial destruction
questions.explanation: Elijah's letter in verses 12–13 warns Jehoram of judgment due to his evil ways, which he ignores, leading to devastating consequences.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 21:14–19 portrays an unjust God who punishes entire families for one man's sins. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God punishes the innocent without cause as a demonstration of arbitrary power
The passage teaches corporate responsibility and the consequences of sin extending to family and society
God’s punishment is limited strictly to the individual sinner alone
The text excuses Jehoram's sins by blaming his family
questions.correctAnswer: The passage teaches corporate responsibility and the consequences of sin extending to family and society
questions.explanation: Verses 14–19 show that Jehoram's sin results in judgment affecting his family and possessions, reflecting the biblical doctrine of corporate solidarity and consequences of leadership sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 21:3 teach about royal succession and divine election?
options: The kingdom is given to the most pious son regardless of birth order
Succession follows the firstborn, but gifts can be distributed to other sons
The throne is divided equally among all sons
Kingship is determined by popular vote among the people
questions.correctAnswer: Succession follows the firstborn, but gifts can be distributed to other sons
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states that Jehoshaphat gave gifts to his other sons but gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn, illustrating birthright succession.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is manifested in 2 Chronicles 21:19 in relation to the respect or dishonor shown to Jehoram after death?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 19 notes that Jehoram's people made no burning for him like his fathers, showing a form of righteous judgment and dishonor due to his evil reign.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 21:9 contribute to the biblical narrative of divine empowerment for righteous kingship and military success?
options: It shows that military success is unrelated to divine favor
It exemplifies God empowering a king to defend his kingdom despite personal sin
It demonstrates that success is purely due to human strategy without divine involvement
It predicts complete military failure due to sin
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies God empowering a king to defend his kingdom despite personal sin
questions.explanation: Verse 9 records Jehoram smiting the Edomites, suggesting God still grants military strength even to a compromised king, showing complexity in divine dealings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 21:17 and 21:20 teach about divine judgment and legacy in the context of kingship?
options: Judgment eradicates all descendants and erases legacy
Despite judgment, a remnant is preserved, but the king’s legacy is dishonored
Judgment is always reversed quickly preserving full legacy
Kings who sin are always honored equally after death
questions.correctAnswer: Despite judgment, a remnant is preserved, but the king’s legacy is dishonored
questions.explanation: Verse 17 notes only Jehoahaz survived, while verse 20 shows Jehoram was buried without honor, illustrating preservation of lineage but a tarnished legacy.
